what_its_for: Dronedarone is used to help keep your heart beating in a normal, steady rhythm. It is prescribed for people who have had a type of irregular heartbeat called atrial fibrillation (AFib) or atrial flutter, and whose heart rhythm has returned to normal. It helps reduce the chances of your irregular heartbeat coming back and lowers the risk of you needing to be admitted to the hospital for heart rhythm problems.
how_to_take: Take dronedarone by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Always take it WITH food — taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine properly and reduces the chance of stomach upset. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep it working consistently. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets.
dosing: The usual dose for most adults is one 400 mg tablet taken TWICE a day — once with your morning meal and once with your evening meal. Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribed. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to the medication and your other health conditions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose completely and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time with your next meal. Do NOT double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store dronedarone tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Store them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. If you need to dispose of unused medication, ask your pharmacist about a safe drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking this medicine — it can increase the level of dronedarone in your blood to a dangerous level. Do not take dronedarone if you are in permanent atrial fibrillation (where your heart has not returned to a normal rhythm). Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) as it can make dronedarone less effective. Limit or avoid alcohol. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal products, because dronedarone can interact with many medicines, including certain antibiotics, antifungals, and other heart medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or call 911 if you experience: shortness of breath, especially when lying down or with mild activity; sudden weight gain (more than 2 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week); swelling of your legs, ankles, or feet; a new or worsening irregular or rapid heartbeat; feeling faint or passing out; yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (possible signs of liver problems); dry cough, difficulty breathing, or fever (possible signs of lung problems); unusual tiredness or weakness. Also call your doctor before starting, stopping, or changing any other medications while on dronedarone.
when_it_works: Dronedarone starts working shortly after you begin taking it, but you may not feel any different right away since it is working in the background to keep your heart in a normal rhythm and prevent future episodes. It is important to keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well. Your doctor will monitor how well it is working through regular check-ups and tests, such as an EKG (electrocardiogram) and blood tests to check your heart, liver, and kidney function.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Dronedarone can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed while taking dronedarone, as it may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. OLDER ADULTS: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects; your doctor will monitor you closely. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: This medication is NOT recommended for people with severe liver disease. Your doctor will check your liver function with blood tests before and during treatment. Tell your doctor about any history of liver or kidney problems. CHILDREN: Dronedarone is not approved for use in children and teenagers under 18 years of age.
